knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 4.2.6
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly defines deviance, scaled deviance, and what is estimated in a GLM?
knowledge_checks.body: Select the deviance and estimation statement.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Deviance is a likelihood comparison to saturated fit. Mechanical p-value deletion is model choice, not deviance definition. GLM estimation is typically MLE/IWLS.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Deviance compares to saturated; scaled divides by scale; estimate by MLE/IWLS.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating p-value chopping as deviance definition or moment matching as GLM estimation.

choices.label: Deviance compares the fitted model log-likelihood to a saturated model. Scaled deviance divides by dispersion or scale when relevant. GLM parameters are typically estimated by maximum likelihood (often via IWLS).
Deleting insignificant terms until p-values look nice defines deviance and finishes GLM estimation.
Deviance equals the sum of Pearson residuals by definition; scaled deviance is always the same number without dividing by scale.
GLM parameters are estimated by equating sample moments to population moments; deviance is an optional display label.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 4.2.6
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly defines deviance and scaled deviance and names the usual GLM estimation principle?
knowledge_checks.body: One sentence each; refuse p-value chopping.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Deviance is twice the log-likelihood drop to saturated. Scale enters scaled deviance when dispersion matters. p-value chopping is not estimation.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Deviance 2(ℓ_sat - ℓ_model); scaled divides by scale; MLE/IWLS. Refuse p-chopping.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Accepting p-value chopping as deviance or estimation definition.

choices.label: Deviance compares the fitted model's log-likelihood to a saturated model (2 times ℓ_sat minus ℓ_model). Scaled deviance divides by dispersion or scale when relevant. Parameters are typically estimated by maximum likelihood (often via IWLS). Mechanical p-value chopping is model-choice behaviour, not deviance definition.
Deviance is the difference in AIC between nested models; scaled deviance is AIC divided by n. Estimation means dropping terms with p greater than 0.10.
Deviance equals sum (y minus μ̂) squared; scaled deviance adds sigma hat. GLM parameters are always OLS slopes on the link scale.
Deviance and scaled deviance are identical for Poisson and binomial because scale is always 1 with no further definition.
